reader.notes: EmitUnstring tests ptr < 1 || ptr > src.Length before any transfer and, after the receivers, ptr <= src.Length for unexamined characters; the 2002+ zero-length guard is the DialectBehavior row whose 85 arm is off, which is right for the 1985 text. All probes matched.

refuter.evidence: GR17a names only 'the value in the data item referenced by identifier-7'; with no POINTER phrase there is no identifier-7, and GR13a says only that examination begins 'with the leftmost character position'. GR17b needs unexamined characters, which a zero-size sender lacks. So at 1985 an UNSTRING with no POINTER from a zero-size sender meets neither GR17 condition and GR20 sends control to NOT ON OVERFLOW. StringEmitter.cs#EmitUnstring (lines 236-247) writes 'long ptr = 1;' when POINTER is omitted and then tests 'ptr < 1 || ptr > src.Length', so the absent identifier-7 is treated as 1 and a zero-size sender becomes an overflow. Probe r4_nopointer_zero.cob (OG = OCCURS 0 TO 8 DEPENDING ON WC, WC=0; UNSTRING OG DELIMITED BY "," INTO WX TALLYING IN WT, no POINTER): --std 85 printed 'C OVERFLOW / C X=[QQQ] T=00' (runs/r4_nopointer_zero-001); --std 2023 printed neither phrase (2023 GR2 guard). The witness pb5816_unstring_zero_length_sender_overflow leg C expects 'C OVERFLOW' on 'the implicit pointer 1', which the 1985 text does not state; kb/Work PB5816's own repro uses WITH POINTER only. Everything else holds: r4_overflow.cob (runs/r4_overflow-001) ODO sender current size 4 with POINTER 5 overflows and POINTER 4 does not; zero size with explicit POINTER 1 overflows with TALLYING untouched; 'AB,,' into one receiver overflows at PT 4; ALL ',' consumes the trailing commas with no overflow (PT 6); 'AB,,,' into two receivers overflows at PT 5. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR17a  the text is in GR17a'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR17b  the text is in GR17b'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR20  the text is in GR20'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR13a  the text is in GR13a'.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/StringEmitter.cs#EmitUnstring: the POINTER-absent arm ('long ptr = 1') feeds the GR17a initiation test at every edition; at 85 the test must apply only when identifier-7 is written (the 85 arm of DialectBehavior.UnstringZeroLengthSenderTerminates removes the guard but nothing restricts GR17a to identifier-7)
refuter.corrected: PARTIAL (wrong-answer, cause c: 1985 GR17a covers less than the code applies, only a written POINTER item). At --std 85, UNSTRING with no POINTER from a zero-size identifier-1 must not raise overflow; the ON OVERFLOW imperative runs where GR20 requires NOT ON OVERFLOW. With POINTER, every GR17a and GR17b case probed conforms. The pb5816 witness's leg C expectation must change with the fix. Known note: kb/Work PB5816 (landed) introduced the behaviour; its repro and text cover only the POINTER form.

adjudication.reason: At `--std 85` an UNSTRING with NO POINTER phrase from a zero-size sender runs ON OVERFLOW, where the 1985 text gives NOT ON OVERFLOW. The fix of kb/Work PB5816 carried the ruling made for WITH POINTER to the form with no POINTER, and leg C of its witness expects the wrong answer.
